audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts give Singed six of seven stages, and diff is FAV 4/10 — but the entry's own whys call levels 1, 2, 3 and 6 even and hand first item to Nasus, and the Emerald+ rate is only 52.15% over 1584 games.
audit.why: whys[0] 'Neither kit has a decisive level-1 edge', whys[2] 'making this a genuine skill matchup', whys[4] 'a coin-flip', whys[5] 'he owns this window'. The audit packet levelChart (Skill / Skill / Skill / Singed / Skill / Nasus / Skill) matches that prose exactly; the shipped chart does not.
audit.corrected: Early: even, no kill pressure either way. Levels 4-5: Singed's proxy window, his only owned stage. Level 6: coin-flip. Sheen first item: Nasus. Side lane and late: even, Singed on macro and Nasus in the 1v1.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the phases[N].why strings are generic template text that never names a Nasus ability.
audit.why: Riot's data: Wither 15/14/13/12/11s at 700 range, Spirit Fire flat 12s at 650, Siphoning Strike 7.5s down to 3.5s, Fury of the Sands 120/100/80s. Insanity Potion is a flat 100s. Those numbers are what make the proxy window concrete.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 are the spike because Wither is a 15s cooldown at rank 1 — the gaps are long enough to run him down. Nasus spikes on Sheen and on Fury of the Sands at 6; you spike on Insanity Potion at 6 and Rylai's.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid and wants.foe[2] both attribute lifesteal to Fury of the Sands, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds appears nowhere in either layer despite the entry leaning on Nasus's sustain three times. The 575-unit gap between Wither (700) and Fling (125) is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text for Fury of the Sands lists increased Health, Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown — no lifesteal. The lifesteal is Soul Eater, the passive. Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, which is the direct counter to that passive and the reason the level-6 fight is a coin-flip rather than a loss. Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: His sustain is Soul Eater, not the ultimate — pop Insanity Potion first so Poison Trail applies Grievous Wounds and the lifesteal stops carrying him. Wither reaches 700 and Fling only 125, so he always lands his first. Watch the Siphoning Strike auto-reset wind-up, not the cast.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your best pure-agency window in this lane. Nasus has no chase tool and Wither has a punishing cooldown at early ranks — whenever you see it used on a minion or on cooldown, you can run directly through him, Fling, and Mega Adhesive him into the trail. More importantly, start proxying the wave between his tower and the mid-river: Nasus cannot clear it fast enough to both defend his tower and follow you, so he is forced to stand still and watch stacks evaporate. At level 6 Insanity Potion makes you tanky enough to absorb more punishment, but Nasus's ultimate simultaneously gives him lifesteal and size that let him sustain through your gas in extended fights — do not overstay a 1v1 unless you are certain Wither is on cooldown. Force short burst trades: run through, Fling, disengage before Wither comes back up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your best pure-agency window in this lane. Nasus has no chase tool and Wither has a punishing cooldown at early ranks — whenever you see it used on a minion or on cooldown, you can run directly through him, Fling, and Mega Adhesive him into the trail. More importantly, start proxying the wave between his tower and the mid-river: Nasus cannot clear it fast enough to both defend his tower and follow you, so he is forced to stand still and watch stacks evaporate. At level 6 Insanity Potion makes you tanky enough to absorb more punishment, but Fury of the Sands gives him Health, resistances and a faster Q, and Soul Eater heals it all back unless your R is up — do not overstay a 1v1 unless you are certain Wither is on cooldown. Force short burst trades: run through, Fling, disengage before Wither comes back up.

edits.before: Both ultimates reshape the 1v1 simultaneously — Insanity Potion gives Singed the stats to run at Nasus, but Fury of the Sands gives Nasus lifesteal and size to sustain, making the direct fight a coin-flip decided by Wither timing.
